days.d: Related by blood
f: Related by marriage
Bound by oath
Raised together
days.r: Latin cōnsanguineus, from con- “together” + sanguis “blood”
days.s: Am not I consanguineous? am I not of her blood?

days.d: A visible (but not necessarily material) manifestation of a deity to a human person
f: A violent (but usually brief) storm accompanied by thunder, hail, and high winds
A public (but not necessarily religious) celebration in honour of a god or hero
A sudden (but not necessarily accurate) insight into the meaning of a dream or omen
days.r: Late Latin theophania, from Greek theós “God” + phaínō “to shine, appear”
days.s: It was a bewildering theophany, since it was impossible to make out anything clearly in the stormy obscurity of thunder, lightning, smoke and wind.

days.d: A large galleon sailed in the Mediterranean as a merchantman
f: A long oared galley rowed in the Mediterranean by convicts
A flat-bottomed barge towed along the Nile as a ferry
A light three-masted vessel sailed in the Atlantic as a fishing boat
days.r: French caraque, from Latin carrus “wagon”; or perhaps from Arabic qarāqīr
days.s: Thereafter huge sailing carracks brought Indian pepper and cotton, Indonesian perfume and spice, Chinese silk and porcelain, to the royal trading house at Lisbon.

days.d: A woman’s silk or lace scarf
f: A heavy woollen blanket
A woman’s quilted silk jacket
A woman’s fur-trimmed travelling coat
days.r: Spanish mantilla “large veil; small cape”, from manta “blanket, cloth”
days.s: The Duchess of Alba wrapped herself in a mantilla coat.

days.d: Indicator provided by the stationary arm whose shadow indicates the time on the sundial
f: Indicator provided by the hand of a clock that marks the passing minutes
Indicator provided by the needle of a compass that points to magnetic north
Indicator provided by the float of a water clock that rises as the vessel fills
days.r: Greek gnṓmōn “discerner, interpreter; carpenter’s square”
days.s: The little style or gnomon, which being fixed on the pole of the globe, and turning round with it, points out the hours upon the hour circle.

days.d: Full of trivial conversation
f: Full of stern disapproval
Full of anxious worry
Full of quiet satisfaction
days.r: Latin garrulus “talkative”, from garriō “to chatter”
days.s: She lingered for a few moments, and was garrulous over some detail of the household.

days.d: Stubbornly persistent in wrongdoing
f: Gently forgiving of wrongdoing
Easily swayed by flattery
Deeply weary of duty
days.r: Latin obdūrātus “hardened”, from ob- “against” + dūrō “to harden”
days.s: But custom maketh blind and obdurate The loftiest hearts.

days.d: Having the power to prevent evil or bad luck
f: Having the power to reveal hidden truths
Having the power to command the dead
Having the power to stir up strong emotion
days.r: Greek apotrópaios, from apó “away” + trópos “turn”: “turning away evil”
days.s: A boring subtext, about the wisdom or otherwise of actually uttering Voldemort's name, meanwhile robs the apotropaic device of its force.

(of liquids) frothing and bubbling as with boiling
(of liquids) tinted a deep colour as with dye

days.s: This makes the estimation of the refractive index of the turbid liquid quite problematic.
